sheet-53.description: The southern of the three Mantoloking sheets, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It covers the narrow barrier beach between Barnegat Bay on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east, from Princeton Avenue at the top down to an east-west street lettered only 'Street' (today's Albertson Street) and the beginning of the next row of blocks below it. Bay Avenue runs along the bay shore, which is drawn as a winding blue band cutting into the westernmost block; the Pennsylvania Railroad runs on its own right of way just east of Bay Avenue, and Ocean Avenue runs parallel to it further east. The eastern row of blocks is lettered as reaching 110 feet to the Atlantic Ocean, which is not drawn. The blocks are numbered 1A to 6A. Development is very sparse: a handful of frame dwellings on lots 101, 102, 119, 120 and 122, two small buildings marked for storage of furniture near the bay, and the large frame hotel The Albertson on Ocean Avenue, noted as closed March 25, 1905. Most lots are empty and only some carry lot numbers. A compass rose stands in the bay. The upper right of the sheet carries the atlas title, the population note (winter 25, summer 1000; no water facilities, no fire department), a key map of the three sheets and the legend; these lie outside the georeferenced area. A scale bar sits at the bottom left.
notes: The unnamed 'Street' at the bottom of the sheet is today's Albertson Street.
Bay Avenue south of Princeton Avenue no longer exists under that name; its line is followed by the north-south leg of Carpenter Lane and by Runyon Lane south of Albertson Street.
The Pennsylvania Railroad line through Mantoloking has been removed.
The Albertson hotel is marked closed March 25, 1905.

Scale 60 ft to an inch. South end: Bay Av, Ocean Av and the Pennsylvania R.R. between Princeton Av and an unnamed 'Street' (today Albertson Street). Title block and a key map of the three sheets (not to scale) right of the heavy line are masked out; the main map is one part.

sheet-54.description: The middle Mantoloking sheet, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It runs from Princeton Avenue at the bottom to Ashton Avenue (today Downer Avenue) at the top, across the barrier beach from Barnegat Bay on the west to the Atlantic Ocean, whose shoreline is drawn as a blue band along the east edge. Bay Avenue follows the bay shore and jogs west at Arnold, a short street running from Bay Avenue to the bay. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs north-south between Bay Avenue and Ocean Avenue; beside it stand the depot and dwelling, a freight house and an ice house. This is the village centre: a grocery and post office on Bay Avenue at Ashton Avenue, a carpenter shop and a boat house on the bay side, a pumping station with gasoline engine pump, three domestic-supply water tanks and an elevated water tank on block 2A, and the Episcopal church on Ocean Avenue. Frame dwellings line the east side of the eastern block row (block 4A) facing the ocean, with others on Bay Avenue and Ocean Avenue. At the top left a lagoon is drawn with a building on a pier reached by a walkway from Ashton Avenue. Blocks are numbered 1A to 5A, with lot numbers. A compass rose stands in the bay and a scale bar at the bottom right; the neighbouring sheets 53 and 55 are referenced in the margins.
notes: Ashton Avenue is today's Downer Avenue.
Arnold has no counterpart in OpenStreetMap; modern Bay Avenue bends where the sheet shows Bay Avenue jogging at Arnold.
The Pennsylvania Railroad line through Mantoloking has been removed.
Scale 60 ft to an inch. Princeton Av to Ashton Av (today Downer Avenue); Bay Av jogs west at Arnold (Arnold not in OpenStreetMap). Depot, Episcopal church, water tanks. One part.

sheet-55.description: The northern Mantoloking sheet, drawn at 60 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. It covers the barrier beach from Ashton Avenue (today Downer Avenue) at the bottom to Herbert Avenue (today Herbert Street) and the blocks beyond it at the top. Barnegat Bay fills the west side, its shore curving in towards Bay Avenue in the north. West of Bay Avenue are Bridge, from which a wooden bridge crosses the bay westward, and Lake St.; south of Lake St. a pond enclosed by a curving shore is marked 'being filled in', and a club house stands on a pier at the bay end of Ashton Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs north-south between Bay Avenue and Ocean Avenue, and the eastern block row is lettered as reaching 110 feet to the Atlantic Ocean. Blocks are numbered 1A to 10A and lots are numbered throughout. Building is sparse: frame dwellings on the bay-side lots by Bridge, on Bay Avenue (including a studio), a dwelling at the bay shore by Herbert Avenue, and a row of frame dwellings on the ocean-side block between Ashton and Herbert avenues; most lots are empty. A compass rose stands in the bay at the upper left, and a scale bar at the bottom left; the neighbouring sheet 54 is referenced at the bottom.
notes: Herbert Avenue is today's Herbert Street; Ashton Avenue is today's Downer Avenue; Bridge is today's Old Bridge Street.
Lake St. corresponds to a service road named Lake Street in OpenStreetMap, which does not match the drawn line (12 m off) and was not used.
The wooden bridge across Barnegat Bay at Bridge has been replaced by the Mantoloking Bridge on Herbert Street (CR 528).
Scale 60 ft to an inch. Ashton Av (Downer Avenue) to Herbert Av (Herbert Street); Bridge (Old Bridge Street) and Lake St west of Bay Av, wooden bridge, club house. One part.
